commit.message: release(dsh): 0.1.6-alpha.2
fix(creator): address plugin workflow review findings
test(plugin-manager): keep approval assertions type-safe
fix(plugin-manager): request approval for single-call full access
fix(plugin-manager): require full access for agent tool calls
feat(creator): use Plugin Manager for persistent plugins

refactor(plugins): name bundles by their package name only

`dsh.title` was a manifest field this branch introduced: the manager read
it for `listBundles` and `inspect`, and the Web page showed it over the
package name. A bundle is named by its package name now, so `DshManifest`
keeps only its shipped fields, the page derives every heading from the
name, and the install dialog's subject line reads the name the Host
answered. The two e2e fixtures drop their titles and the manager lane's
goldens follow.

refactor(plugins): read a bundle's one-liner from the package description only

The dsh manifest gains no description field: a bundle's card shows the
package.json description, and the shipped optional bundles carry no
display title or description of their own until localized metadata is
designed. The plugin author tutorial shows the bundle declaration alone.

refactor(plugins): name the optional bundles in the launcher, not the installation manifest

OPTIONAL_BUNDLES in app-boot lists the bundles the installation ships
switched off; the plugin manager, the default-product isolation gate,
the workspace constraints, and the packed-install check read that one
list instead of a dsh.optionalBundles field in apps/cli/package.json.

refactor(plugins): stop announcing patch generations applied outside the manager

app-boot no longer emits profile/reconciled after a reload, and the plugin
manager no longer turns such a generation into a plugin-manager/changed
notice: the Web page learns of a CLI or hand edit on its next read. The
change event keeps only the reasons a manager operation produces.

feat(plugins): ship optional bundles switched off and guide the install dialog

The dsh installation lists under `dsh.optionalBundles` the bundles it
ships for a person to switch on. The plugin manager reports them as
`optional`, and the Web plugin page shows them first, in a built-in
group with an official tag, off until selected and never removable.
Agent Teams ships this way, so a blank profile offers both of its
layers. Default-product isolation, the workspace constraints, and the
packed-install check accept that one dependency edge and nothing else
experimental.

A bundle's title and one-liner come from `dsh.title` and the new
`dsh.description`, else from the package name and `description`. A
dependency without a bundle patch is no longer listed unless the
profile selects it. The install dialog asks for a package name or
address; a guide under the field shows the three accepted forms with
an example each and ends in a security warning, and the copy no longer
speaks of a plugin ID.

Merge remote-tracking branch 'origin/master' into feat/plugin-mgmt-4-web

Master now carries the final #4182 plugin manager and the live client
module graph of #4189, so the web management layer is re-ported onto
them:

- The manager keeps master's `ManagementError` codes, `ChangeResult`
  stages, `configure()` under `hmr.runExclusive`, `reload()` warnings
  and `writePluginEnabled` name matching, and adds back `inspect`,
  request-id installs with `plugin-manager/install-log` and
  `plugin-manager/install-state`, `cancelInstall`, `listBundles` titles,
  rows and overrides, `packageResult.kind`, `pnpmCommand` and
  `inspectTimeoutMs`, and `plugin-manager/changed` after each change and
  each `profile/reconciled`. A failed or cancelled installation restores
  the snapshotted manifest and lockfile instead of master's one-shot
  `pnpm remove` cleanup, so `cleanup` and `remainingDependencies` leave
  the result.
- App boot keeps master's reconciliation diagnostics and emits
  `profile/reconciled`; `watchUserPatches` goes with the launcher's
  watcher now that HMR owns profile reloads.
- The settings Plugin list tab stays read-only with #4189's page-local
  sync failures and retry; master's bundle form and row checkboxes are
  dropped again. The sidebar page words the Host's codes through its
  dictionary, and a client bundle change follows the live module graph
  without a page reload.
- The web e2e scaffold no longer chooses a reload policy: the base
  bundle's `hmr` row turns on with the profile context and application
  readiness, and `profile.hmr: false` disables it through an overlay for
  the startup-only scenario.

feat(web): manage plugins over the #4182 manager from the sidebar page

The sidebar Plugins page now drives `ctx.pluginManager` from #4182 and the
settings Plugin list tab goes back to read-only: its bundle form and row
checkboxes are removed, and the page joins `listBundles` with
`listPlugins` into one view per bundle, decides availability from the
inventory's `managementAvailable`, switches bundles and rows through
`setBundleEnabled` and `setPluginEnabled`, and confirms uninstalls.

The manager gains what the guided install dialog needs: `inspect(spec)`
reads a spec through the registry or a directory before anything installs
and refuses specs without a bundle; `installBundle` takes a request id,
streams each pnpm run as `plugin-manager/install-log`, reports its phases
as `plugin-manager/install-state`, classifies a failed run into
`packageResult.kind`, names the bundle it added, and restores
`package.json` and `pnpm-lock.yaml` when the run fails, is cancelled, or
adds a package without a bundle patch; `cancelInstall(requestId)` answers
only after pnpm exited and the files are back; `listBundles` carries
titles, one-liners, declared rows with their live entries, and the
built-in rows a bundle overrides; every completed operation and every
patch generation applied outside the manager emits
`plugin-manager/changed`. The config gains `pnpmCommand` and
`inspectTimeoutMs`. App boot emits `profile/reconciled` after each applied
patch generation and finds a root Include mounted under its pinned id by
another copy of the module.

Row diagnostics, dependency checks, and the non-bundle dependency group
are not carried over; the web e2e scaffold mounts a launcher-style
managed profile instead of the removed profile runtime.
